surfaces.part: reed stalks (olive green vertical blades with pale frost tips)
ice patch at base (light cyan strip)

answer.evidence: The object is a cluster of thin vertical reed stalks 1-5 px wide (rows 0-14) with pale frost tips, standing on a 1-row ice strip at row 15 (width 11). The stalks are drawn as vertical faces with no horizontal band, front-edge line, eave shadow, or ellipse. The ice strip is a single row, so it is only a rim. Reeds are organic, so a flat top is not expected, but there is no top surface to measure: main_top_rows is 0, and the drawing reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sparse cluster of frozen reeds, much smaller than one 16x16 tile, with only 7 distinct colours in total. It has about 3 tones (pale blue-white stalks, a mid tone and a small base highlight). The references are full trees with 6-7 visible tones per tile (tree-1a786c) and 29 (tree-d43edd), layered leaf clumps, shaded trunks and dark-tone outlines. The candidate has no outline, no clumped foliage and no grain, so it looks thinner and flatter than either reference. The per-tile density fact is 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. By eye it is clearly thinner than the reference plants and has too few shading steps. Thin or sparse objects are not failed for sparseness alone, but this one also has shallow shading and no texture variation, so a careful artist would not accept it next to the references.
